title: Desktop spike: Electron shell, engine helper process, plugin hosting, signed macOS build
goal: Prove the process model and plugin hosting on Windows and macOS: Electron starts the engine helper, the UI connects with the token handshake, third-party VST3 and AU plugins load, save and restore state, report latency and open editors, and a signed and notarized macOS build runs.
done: JUCE desktop audio device (#20) covers the device half of JUCE hosting.
Electron shell and engine helper process (#47).
JUCE plugin hosting in the engine, on all three platforms in CI (#48).

Status corrected to in_progress 2026-11-09 (Fable, delegated by the maintainer): m0-electron-shell and m0-plugin-hosting are merged and green in CI; m0-macos-bundle is not built (no helper bundle, no signing job) and waits on the apple-signing gate, so M0 is neither not_started nor exit_pending.
prerequisites: M3 protocol server (the renderer connects through it).

humanGates.text: Create a Developer ID Application certificate and a notarization API key in the maintainer's Apple Developer account, and approve storing them as GitHub Actions secrets.
humanGates.how: The maintainer logs in; Claude can drive the portal through Claude in Chrome with the maintainer present, and must ask before storing any secret.

humanGates.text: Judge editor-window focus and Cmd-Tab behaviour on a real Mac.
humanGates.how: The maintainer runs the signed build on a Mac and records the result; CI cannot judge window behaviour. Open the editor through the protocol (since M4: plugin.instantiate, then plugin.open_editor {slotId}; the engine's --open-editor flag and the shell's SIANN_OPEN_EDITOR are gone). Check, with an editor open: clicking the Electron window leaves the editor visible; Cmd-Tab lists the engine as an app and returns to it; Cmd-Tab to a third application shows the editor floating above it (the behaviour under judgement); minimise and restore the editor; Electron in fullscreen (the editor carries FullScreenAuxiliary, so it should join that space). Note while judging: the engine never calls [NSApp finishLaunching] (JUCE's loop runs without it), so record any activation, menu-bar or focus oddity that could stem from that. Also open a CLAP editor (siann_test_plugin's CLAP, or Surge XT's .clap through plugin.instantiate and plugin.open_editor; m5-clap-editor-window) and check it floats and takes focus like the VST3 one. Record acceptable / acceptable only with conditional floating / unacceptable.

humanGates.text: Name one third-party VST3 and one AU plugin installed on the maintainer's machines for the hosting tests.
humanGates.how: The maintainer lists them; tests read their paths from SIANN_TEST_VST3 and SIANN_TEST_AU and SKIP with a message naming the variable when it is unset, and fail when it points at a missing file.
humanGates.resolvedBy: Fable consultation, delegated by the maintainer
humanGates.resolution: Windows VST3: TDR Nova (Tokyo Dawn Records; free, no account or licence server, has an editor, reports 184 frames of latency at 48 kHz) at C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3\TDR Nova.vst3. macOS AU: TDR Nova AU from the same free installer at /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/Components/TDR Nova.component (the maintainer installs it on the Mac). Fallback for either: TDR VOS SlickEQ. CI downloads no third-party plugins: the desktop job builds siann_test_plugin (JUCE; VST3 on all runners, AU on macOS) with a fixed declared latency switchable by a parameter and a versioned state blob, hosted through a compile-time path (SIANN_TEST_PLUGIN_VST3 / SIANN_TEST_PLUGIN_AU) so that test never skips; macOS CI also hosts Apple AUPeakLimiter as a foreign-vendor AU. Third-party state round-trips compare parameter values, not raw blobs. The third-party tests run only on the maintainer machines and gate m0-exit-plugins. Corrected 2026-11-07: Nova's latency does not change at runtime (184 frames in every mode, 4 values on each of its 75 parameters, no latency-change event), so the runtime latency change is proven on siann_test_plugin only; the third-party plugins prove load, state, reported latency against an impulse, and the editor.

features.title: Electron app under app/ that spawns and supervises the engine helper
acceptance: app/ holds an Electron app (TypeScript, contextIsolation on, nodeIntegration off) that starts the engine helper, restarts it with crash-loop backoff and passes port and token to the renderer through preload.
Playwright (Electron) tests start the app, see the renderer connect with the token handshake, kill the engine and see it restart, and quit the app and see the engine process gone (no orphan).

features.title: JUCE plugin hosting in the engine helper
acceptance: JucePluginHost implements PluginHost: scan, instantiate on the main thread, process on the audio thread with no SIANN lock (JUCE's wrapper locks inside processBlock are the accepted exception in the spec's "Realtime rules and enforcement", ADR-0018), state get/set as blobs, latency and capability reporting.

Hosting tests load the maintainer VST3 (and AU on macOS) from SIANN_TEST_VST3 / SIANN_TEST_AU and the CI-built siann_test_plugin; all save and restore state, read latency and open and close the editor. The runtime latency change, and the restart during playback, are proven on siann_test_plugin, whose latency is switched by a parameter; no third-party runtime latency change is required.
Windows editors are owned by the Electron window via GWLP_HWNDPARENT; macOS editors float and the engine activates itself.

The graph driver counts device callbacks over their period (xruns: slow callbacks, never device-reported xruns), the longest callback and callbacks it could not check, on the audio thread with atomics only; siann-cli play and record report them as xruns, maxCallbackMicros and unmeasuredCallbacks, and a known miss driven through --fake-callback-nanos reaches the JSON. In M0 no shipped path processes a hosted plugin (no graph node wraps a PluginInstance; siann-engine runs no device), so the counter does not yet show a plugin's wait: that holds once the M4 plugin node calls process() from a driver callback, and the protocol carries the three counters once the engine process runs a device (spec, "Realtime rules and enforcement"; ADR-0018 amendment).

features.title: macOS helper app bundle, hardened runtime, signing and notarization in CI
acceptance: The engine ships as SIANN.app/Contents/Helpers/SIANN Engine.app with LSUIElement=1 and com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation.
A macOS CI job signs with the Developer ID certificate and notarizes with the API key from secrets, then verifies with spctl and stapler.

exit.text: Engine starts and stops with the app; the renderer connects with the token handshake.
One third-party VST3 and one AU load, save and restore state, report latency and open editors.
exit.how: Hosting tests on the maintainer machines with SIANN_TEST_VST3 and SIANN_TEST_AU set; CI runs the same tests against siann_test_plugin and Apple AUPeakLimiter.

exit.text: A signed and notarized macOS build runs; focus and Cmd-Tab behaviour is acceptable.
exit.how: CI notarization plus the maintainer's hands-on check (human gate), with the editor opened through plugin.instantiate and plugin.open_editor.

killCriterion: No acceptable editor-window behaviour on macOS after two weeks, with unconditional floating (NSFloatingWindowLevel) and conditional floating (float only while Electron or the engine is frontmost) both tried: evaluate engine-in-main-process or Tracktion with the maintainer.
